barriers.description: Across >70 scraped reviews there is a complete absence of any mention of “wishlist”, “save for later”, “save”, or related phrasing. Users repeatedly praise the app’s overall experience but never reference the act of bookmarking items, indicating that the wishlist UI is either not visible, not intuitive, or not perceived as valuable enough to mention. This low salience prevents users from forming the habit of saving items, which in turn eliminates the observable pre‑purchase intent signals the research seeks.

Jobs‑to‑be‑done analysis reveals a functional need: “When I discover a product I like but cannot purchase immediately, I want a simple way to remember it for future reference.” Yet the review data provides no explicit signals of DEFERRED_PURCHASE intent, implying that users either do not articulate this need in reviews or the app does not surface a mechanism (e.g., reminders, scheduler) that makes the intent visible. The hidden intent means the product team cannot identify or address the underlying reasons users postpone buying, such as salary timing or occasion planning.

jobs.job_statement: When I discover a product I like but cannot purchase immediately, I want a simple way to remember it for future reference, so I can revisit it when I have the right occasion, budget, or confidence in fit.
jobs.current_solution: Users appear to rely on mental notes or external tools (e.g., screenshots) because the app’s wishlist is not mentioned as a solution in any review.
gaps: Lack of visible or compelling wishlist UI that prompts users to save items.
No expressed confidence that saved items will remain available or accurately represent fit later.

opportunities.title: Proactive Wishlist Prompt on Product Detail
opportunities.description: Display a subtle, context‑aware ‘Save for later’ button the moment a user scrolls past key product attributes, coupled with a brief tooltip explaining that saved items stay available for 30 days.
opportunities.recommended_experiment: A/B test two variants: (A) static heart icon, (B) animated save prompt with tooltip. Measure add‑to‑wishlist rate and subsequent conversion within 14 days.

opportunities.title: Wishlist Visibility Dashboard
opportunities.description: Create a persistent ‘My Saves’ badge on the bottom navigation that shows count of saved items and a quick‑access carousel, reducing clutter perception and encouraging review.
opportunities.recommended_experiment: Introduce the badge to 20% of users and track wishlist‑to‑purchase conversion versus control.

opportunities.title: Deferred Purchase Scheduler
opportunities.description: Allow users to tag saved items with a future reminder (e.g., ‘Buy in 2 weeks’) and optionally set a calendar notification, supporting DEFERRED_PURCHASE intent.
opportunities.recommended_experiment: Pilot the scheduler for a subset of power users; monitor reminder click‑through and eventual purchase.

opportunities.title: Multi‑Payment Integration
opportunities.description: Add additional popular payment gateways (UPI, credit‑card wallets) to eliminate the sole‑payment‑method barrier observed in the payment‑limited segment.
opportunities.recommended_experiment: Roll out new payment options to 5% of traffic and compare checkout completion rates.

hypotheses.statement: The wishlist feature is either under‑used or not salient enough for users to mention in reviews, resulting in a scarcity of explicit wishlist intent signals.
hypotheses.rationale: Across 70+ reviews, zero mentions of "wishlist", "save for later", "save", "later" or any phrasing that would indicate pre‑purchase saving behavior.

hypotheses.statement: When users do experience pre‑purchase friction, it is more likely to be monetary (payment method) than non‑monetary (fit, trend, clutter), which aligns with the research scope of excluding price‑related drop‑off.
hypotheses.rationale: The only pre‑purchase friction observed is a complaint about limited payment options (PhonePe). No fit‑uncertainty, trend‑decay, wishlist‑clutter, or stock‑sensitivity language appears.
